description: We are Interstellar Nexus, a team of six passionate young minds fascinated by space, science, and technology. Taking on NASA's "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, we aim to uncover hidden stories through research, creativity, and innovation. United by curiosity, teamwork, and a determination to excel, we are here to learn, gain hands-on experience, push boundaries, and transform ambitious ideas into meaningful solutions. We don't just explore the unknown; we strive to make a difference.
summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is a 3D storytelling web atlas created with Three.js, GSAP ScrollTrigger, Lenis and Web Speech synthesis. It records thirty‑four human‑made spacecraft sites on the Moon and Mars twenty‑two on the Moon and twelve on Mars from 1959 to the day.

Abandoned but not Forgotten shows how to solve this problem. Visitors start inside a black hole sequence and watch a rocket launch. They then scroll through a five‑stage Apollo prologue. Can explore interactive 3D globes of the Moon and Mars. They can inspect 3D models of spacecraft view a 2D/3D coordinate atlas and follow a timeline. Mr. Whisper, a voice‑reactive black hole archivist avatar tells the story of each artifact explains what remains on the surface and why it was abandoned. The stories cover Apollo descent stages, sample returners that saved weight, frozen solar landers and one‑way rovers.

Abandoned but not Forgotten is important because lunar and Martian exploration is growing faster. Historic landing sites are more at risk of being disturbed. By mapping and explaining humanity’s off‑world hardware the project turns debris into shared planetary heritage. It sparks curiosity and encourages responsible stewardship, beyond Earth.
details: Abandoned but not Forgotten is a 3D web atlas built with HTML5, CSS3, ES-Module JavaScript, GLSL shaders, Three.js, GSAP ScrollTrigger, Lenis, Vite and the Web Speech API that maps and tells the stories of 34 human-made spacecraft sites resting across the Moon and Mars from 1959 to today. Visitors enter through a GLSL black hole sequence and 4K rocket launch scroll through a 5-stage vector Apollo prologue and explore interactive 3D lunar and Martian globes, inspectable 3D spacecraft models, a filterable 2D/3D coordinate atlas and a horizontal scroll-tide timeline—all guided by Mr. Whisper, a creative voice-reactive black hole avatar who narrates each artifact’s mission history, hardware left behind and the engineering reasons why it had to stay. Designed with off-screen WebGL pausing, adaptive resolution scaling, static fallbacks, live voice captions, verified coordinates and full open-license attributions this zero-install static site makes space science engaging and accessible while fostering awareness and stewardship for preserving humanity’s, off-world heritage.
